about: CS45's story beats: five per temperament, at 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 hearts of your affinity with her. Each is one arc in five steps. Her name is filled at run time; no Uma is named here. A premise alone is the outline layer; lines make it scripted. Clever's five are the prototype (D40).

beats.title: Done Already
beats.premise: She races through her rows before breakfast and asks what’s next, a little out of breath and very pleased.

beats.title: Never a Whole Season
beats.premise: Resting at the Gate, she admits she has never stayed anywhere a whole season; something always looked faster further on.

beats.title: The Dawn Path
beats.premise: She shows you the shortcut she found through the Woods at dawn, and slows down so you can keep up.

beats.title: Sitting Still
beats.premise: She sits still beside you through a whole sunrise, and is surprised to find she liked it.

beats.title: Somewhere to Come Back To
beats.premise: She says the farm is the first place she has ever wanted to run back to, not away from.

beats.title: First at the Gate
beats.premise: You come out early and she is already there, as she has been every morning, rain or shine.

beats.title: The Weather Book
beats.premise: She shows you the notebook where she writes the weather down each day, and what it told her about the turnips.

beats.title: Being Useful
beats.premise: She admits she keeps busy because she is afraid of being forgotten if she isn’t useful.

beats.title: A Day Off
beats.premise: You give her a day off; she spends it on the farm anyway, just not working, and says that counts.

beats.title: Next Season Too
beats.premise: She hands you the weather book’s last page; she has already written the first line of next season.

beats.title: One Post, One Uma
beats.premise: She lifts a fence post on her own to show she can, then asks you to hold the other end anyway.

beats.title: Best of Three
beats.premise: She challenges you to an arm-wrestle on a hay bale, and laughs loudest when she wins.

beats.title: The Broken Pick
beats.premise: She snaps a pick at the Mine and asks you, very quietly, not to tell anyone.

beats.title: Loud on Purpose
beats.premise: She admits she is loud because new people make her nervous, and the farm stopped being new a while ago.

beats.title: On Her Back
beats.premise: She says she would carry the whole farm on her back if it needed her, and means it as a promise.

beats.title: Not in the Rain
beats.premise: She will not stop work for the rain; you end up holding an umbrella over her rows.

beats.title: Out-Fished
beats.premise: A child from town out-fishes her at the Pond, and she swears, cheerfully, to win it back.

beats.title: It’s Nothing
beats.premise: She hurts her hand and insists it is nothing, until you sit her down and bandage it.

beats.title: A Hand Up
beats.premise: For the first time, she asks you for help, and finds it doesn’t feel like losing.

beats.title: The Hardest Thing
beats.premise: She says the hardest thing she ever did was let someone help, and she is glad it was you.

beats.title: The List
beats.premise: She notices you keep a list of everything, and asks to be on it (CS47’s example).

lines.text: You keep a list of everything, don’t you?
Only the important things.
Then put me on it.

beats.title: Third Shelf
beats.premise: She has sorted the Warehouse by a system only she understands, and it works.

lines.text: I sorted the Warehouse. By season, then stars, then price.
I can’t find the turnips.
Spring, two stars, forty gold. Third shelf.
…They’re right there.
Of course they are. I counted.

beats.title: Ten Years
beats.premise: She has drawn up a plan for the farm’s next ten years, and you are in every one of them.

lines.text: I drew up a plan for the farm. Ten years of it.
Ten years?
The Mill in the first, the boat in the second. You’re in all ten.
Am I?
Someone has to read the list.

beats.title: Not on Any List
beats.premise: A rained-out day ruins her plan, and turns into the best afternoon she can remember.

lines.text: It rained all day. Nothing went to plan.
Sorry.
Don’t be. We sat in the barn and talked for hours.
That wasn’t on any list. I’d like to do it again.

beats.title: Lost Count
beats.premise: She used to count her days on the farm, meaning to leave after one season. She has lost count, on purpose.

lines.text: I used to count my days here. One season, then I’d go.
And now?
I lost count somewhere in the second summer.
I don’t think I want to find it again.
